page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-64GB is a Premium family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the system does not support hyperthreading, configured with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 300 GB of local SSD storage. No GPU resources are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with the Geekbench single-core score of 2645.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 39.49 GB/sec both reaching top-tier status. Geekbench text processing also performs in the top tier at 3511.0. Multi-core and general processing metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 44425.64 and Geekbench multi-core score of 17687.0, fall into the average to strong categories. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in low-end LLM text generation, where the 135M model text generation speed is poor at 9.08 tokens per second, though medium 7B model text generation reaches a more typical 13.86 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB RAM per vCPU alongside 300 GB of bundled SSD storage. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for sustained, high-intensity multi-core workloads, but it provides a cost-effective option for bursty or moderately demanding tasks. This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, software compilation, text processing, and database operations that benefit from strong single-core performance and moderate memory capacity.
